weak_signal.why: no measurable association with the target - noise, not signal

redundant.why: carries what a contract feature already carries

review.rule: approved = passed every screen AND an authored entry in feature_config.reason_code_labels. A governance approval is shown as evidence; on its own, without the label, it does not count.

latent_audit.note: Latent columns used to evaluate only - this changes no disposition and no screen. An association near 1 means the attribute is close to a copy of the synthetic truth, which excluding the latent column does not remove.

method.signal: Spearman with sanctioned_rate over all 20,000 population rows (exact, pairwise-complete). Categoricals: bias-corrected Cramer's V against the target, continuous targets binned into deciles.
method.redundancy: Spearman on a 6,000-row sample (seed 42): ranks per column, Pearson over pairwise-complete rows. Contract features are checked against stronger contract features; everything else against every contract feature and every stronger feature already kept, so the stronger of a correlated pair survives. Categoricals: bias-corrected Cramer's V against other categoricals. Categorical-to-numeric redundancy is not measured.
method.stability: PSI between the older and newer halves of the population by application date: ten quantile buckets for numerics (observed levels when ten or fewer), level shares for categoricals. Too few rows reads as not measurable, which does not fail the screen.
method.coverage: share of population rows with a finite value; floor 0.9
method.trend: x - median(x) over applications in the prior 90d (strictly earlier dates, at least 30 of them), computed over the whole application stream - never over an outcome. There is no per-loan history in the data, so this is the market's trend, not the customer's.
method.sentinels: bureau_score: {'below': 0, 'flag': 'new_to_credit', 'display': 'No bureau score (new to credit)'} - from feature_config.yaml (sentinels); read as missing before anything else
method.univariate: Every screen is univariate. A feature that matters only in combination with others can fail the signal screen and still earn its place in a fitted model; the in-model reconciliation is where that shows, and the model's own attributions are the multivariate check.
